page: Amazon Web Services m5d.large is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core across 2 threads. Memory capacity stands at 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 extensions and hardware AES encryption. For direct storage access, it includes a bundled 75 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume. Baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps, and no GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark results position the m5d.large in lower comparative tiers due to its entry-level two-vCPU allocation. In general processing evaluations, the instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 1202.0 and a single-core score of 1013.0, both placing in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested configurations. The PassMark CPU benchmark score recorded 1987.9. Memory bandwidth testing logged uncached read and write speeds of 13.25 GB/sec and 11.42 GB/sec, respectively. In application tests, it delivered 1.65 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and achieved 1.96 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the m5d.large lies in its compute constraints relative to its storage capabilities. While the dedicated single physical core limits multi-threaded scalability and compute-dense processing, the bundled high-speed 75 GB NVMe local storage offers low-latency ephemeral I/O compared to purely network-attached alternatives. This makes the instance cost-efficient for smaller workloads that benefit from fast scratch disks, such as lightweight web servers, development environments, intermediate caching, and microservices requiring low-latency temporary data persistence without substantial parallel compute requirements.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.large is a general-purpose Nitro-based instance equipped with an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at 3.1 GHz. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs (1 physical core), 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 1 Gbps baseline network link, with no GPU acceleration present. A key differentiator is its bundled 75 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, offering low-latency ephemeral storage. Across synthetic benchmarks, the instance reflects its compact core count, registering 1013.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1202.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside 1.65 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. While raw compute and memory throughput sit in lower comparative tiers, the included local NVMe SSD delivers efficient I/O for temporary files, caching, small web serving tasks, and basic development workloads.
